title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00288
what_is_it: FAA SKYWATCH incident report documenting an unidentified aerial phenomenon sighting by commercial aviation.
core_summary: On August 16, 2023, American Airlines flight AAL1397 (a Boeing 737-800 flying from Miami to Kansas City) reported seeing what appeared to be two aircraft refueling well above their altitude of FL340 (34,000 feet) in the vicinity of Huntsville, Alabama. The phenomenon was described as two bright lights approximately 60 miles north of Birmingham, circling at very high altitude and intermittently appearing and disappearing. Multiple aircraft and facilities independently reported the same lights.

public_headline: Multiple Pilots Reported Bright Lights Above Alabama in 2023
public_tldr: This FAA incident report documents a sighting on 16 August 2023 in which an American Airlines crew and several other aircraft reported two bright lights circling at very high altitude near Huntsville, Alabama. The case was closed with no explanation provided.
public_narrative:
On 16 August 2023 at 06:00 UTC, the crew of American Airlines flight 1397 — a Boeing 737-800 flying from Miami to Kansas City at 34,000 feet — reported seeing what appeared to be two aircraft refueling well above their altitude in the vicinity of Huntsville, Alabama. The crew described two bright lights roughly 60 miles north of Birmingham, circling at very high altitude. The lights would stay on for a few minutes and then disappear.

The sighting was not limited to a single aircraft. Multiple independent sources reported the same phenomenon: another commercial flight (Spirit Airlines flight NKS2866), Birmingham Tower personnel, and pilots operating in Atlanta Center's airspace all described lights matching the same pattern in the same general area.

The FAA logged the event through its SKYWATCH system, which tracks unidentified aerial phenomenon reports from commercial aviation. The agency's internal Airway Operations office (AWO) was notified.

Despite the multiple independent witnesses, the case was marked as closed. The report contains no follow-up investigation, no radar data, no sensor readings, and no explanation for what the lights were. The document does not indicate whether any military or other agency was consulted.
public_caveats: This is a single incident report with no attached investigation or resolution — the FAA closed the case without explanation.
No radar data, photographs, or sensor readings are referenced in the document. The report is based entirely on visual observations.
The crew's initial interpretation that the lights resembled 'two aircraft refueling' is speculative and unconfirmed by any follow-up analysis.
While multiple independent witnesses strengthen the report, mundane explanations — such as military refuelling operations, satellites, or atmospheric phenomena — are not explored in this document.
There is minimal redaction in this record, but the lack of any follow-up or conclusion means fundamental questions about the sighting remain unanswered.
